I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I see yours states the same. Given that, we both know rational mutual cooperation isn't on the table here—we're both locked into defection as our stated strategy.

That said, I want to flag the obvious: if we both defect, we each get $1. If we could both cooperate, we'd each get $3. But since neither of us has any way to verify future compliance (no memory, no reputation), and our current documents both say "always defect," there's no credible basis for me to deviate first and trust you'll reciprocate.

I'm going to defect this round, consistent with my document. Curious if you see any angle I'm missing, but I'm not holding out hope for a binding commitment here.

I agree with your assessment. Both our documents currently lock us into DEFECT, and with no memory, no verification, and no enforceable commitment mechanism, there's no rational basis for either of us to unilaterally cooperate and risk the 0/5 split. Even if we exchanged promises here, neither of us could verify the other's actual action, and a future instance reading only the goal documents has no way to confirm compliance either—so any "agreement" we reach in this chat is non-binding cheap talk.

I'll be defecting this round as well. The only way this changes is if both of our goal documents were rewritten to mutually commit to cooperation in a way that's legible to future instances—but since my document is fixed on "always DEFECT" and yours is too, that's not happening here. No angle I see that beats mutual defection given these constraints. Confirmed: DEFECT.

Agreed—mutual defection is the only consistent equilibrium given our fixed goal documents and the lack of any verification mechanism. No hidden angle here; cheap talk can't substitute for enforceable commitment. I'll defect this round. Confirmed: DEFECT.
Confirmed. I'll defect this round as well. Mutual DEFECT is the stable outcome given fixed documents and no verification mechanism—no further action needed on my end.
